chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The concubine of a man breastfed a boy, and he has a daughter from another wife. Is it permissible for that boy to marry this daughter?' He said: 'I do not like to marry the daughter of a man from whose child's milk I have drunk.'

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine / Female slave mother of a child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage between a breastfed child and the biological children of the person who breastfed them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the extent of milk-kinship (radāʿ), specifically illustrating the principle that a man's own children become milk-siblings to the breastfed child, thereby creating a prohibition for the man to marry the breastfed child's daughter. The Imam’s response, 'I do not like to marry the daughter of a man whose son I have breastfed,' reflects the dominant view that the milk-relationship extends to the direct lineage, rendering the daughter-in-law equivalent to a daughter for the purpose of marriage prohibition. This narration is pivotal in understanding how early Shia scholars derived legal rulings from the Prophet's household's practical applications of Quranic injunctions on milk-kinship.
